state.objective: The design question concerns moving /tests plus the test decisions it delegates outside that directory into Can, retiring foreign-language harnesses. The user allows execution other than TypeScript but insists that test code may call unrestricted ordinary Can functions. Only investigation is requested at present. Low-level compiler/runtime services may remain native, whereas moving existing scenarios and comparison rules into such services would fail the requirement.
state.frontend: Go-based checking already constructs Program values containing ordinary functions, assertion bodies, an entry, native signatures and their specializations. The typed intermediate form includes captured functions, calls, preparation steps, completion/error paths, pattern matches and coordination. Both application entries and assertion entries use this checked representation before TypeScript/Bun lowering. A search of the compiler implementation found no general executable Can evaluator.
state.semantics: Running the whole language elsewhere entails matching bigint operations, float identity defined by Object.is, structural/nominal comparisons implemented with Bun.deepEquals, opaque and callable identity, captured bindings, domain/standard failure occurrence identity, queued fixtures and raw exchanges. Async groups and resource owners also need their defined behavior. Both sides of an assertion may execute checked regions. Consequently unrestricted helper support cannot be achieved by interpreting only a list of testing steps.
state.current_execution: The Go assertion controller already bounds concurrent Bun children, handles deadlines and reaping, and reads a protocol specific to assertion roots. It demonstrates available supervisory mechanics but does not implement integration suites. Ordinary Can main can use process::run, file APIs and JSON for live work; attached asserts deliberately prohibit those real effects. Can lacks a general finally, and a timer inside stuck code cannot ensure preemption or teardown on forcible exit.
state.ownership: For all alternatives the Can source is responsible for picking cases, fixture choices, action order, scheduling decisions, expected values, comparisons, result judgments and report policy. Foreign code may implement generic process containment, lifecycle enforcement, hard resource limits and transport, returning crashes or deadlines for Can to judge. A test-plan representation may describe unrestricted function invocations; constraining it to a DSL, implementing only some Can operations or quietly redirecting decisions to host code is unacceptable.
state.gaps: Regardless of executor, missing work includes integration-suite messaging, owned scratch directories, controllable children with descriptors and signals, external browser driving, and independent raw native/database observations. Bindings must perform reusable operations or return observations rather than encapsulate a test and its answer. The current browser::* surface addresses DOM work inside pages, not automation from outside. Switching code generation does not remove these API requirements.
state.trust: Even when a different engine controls testing, candidate fixtures must exercise production TypeScript/Bun compilation and execution to cover compiler/runtime behavior. A second executor separates execution implementations without separating the shared parser, checker or IR. Keep the trusted runner compiler/executor identified by digest separately from the candidate, and retain fixed expected data, deliberately failing controls, and explicit complete/partial/blocked reporting. Alternate execution therefore is not comprehensive oracle independence.
state.limits: Compatibility with previous forms is unnecessary because the project has zero external users. Available laptop storage is 256 GB and sustained load is constrained. Performance tests and wide builds are deferred, leaving comparative startup, CPU and storage improvements unmeasured. Constrain parallel work, durations, logs and disk use, install cleanup as resources are acquired, and recover only inactive owned leftovers. Share builds during one run rather than keep private bundle caches or duplicate dependencies. Favor lower development and ongoing semantic cost subject to unrestricted Can, preserved coverage and safe isolation.

backend.instructions: Choose the most defensible initial test execution design under these facts: helpers use all normal Can, policy and oracles reside in Can, production paths remain exercised, and development/load costs matter. Treat absent capabilities as required work and unmeasured speed as unknown.

criteria.supervised_bun: Execute unrestricted Can tests/helpers using the established TypeScript/Bun compiler path, with a generic native parent providing isolation, limits and owned-resource teardown. Can retains case choreography, scheduling choices and results policy. Separate trusted runner provenance from candidate provenance and implement the necessary bindings/protocol while reusing one language runtime.
criteria.full_ir_interpreter: Create a Go evaluator covering the entire checked Can IR and its platform/native contracts for the test controller and helpers. Contain it externally, identify its trusted version, leave decisions in Can and validate subject programs through their normal TypeScript/Bun output. Choose the extra semantic implementation and maintenance effort in exchange for removing TypeScript compilation of test bodies.
criteria.native_codegen: Add another complete compilation target producing native Can test executables, together with its required runtime and platform layer. Allow every ordinary helper, keep test policy in Can, bound runs and identify the executor, while separately qualifying production TypeScript/Bun subjects. Pay for the wider compiler/backend project as part of the migration.
criteria.undetermined: Withhold an architectural preference because a consequential unresolved fact prevents choosing among these directions; investigate that narrow uncertainty first.
